analysis.title: Fixed Income Weekly Primer (November 16, 2026)
key_insights: Treasury yields rose 21 to 37 basis points across the curve last week. The report attributes the move to renewed inflation concerns and several slightly weaker Treasury auctions.
October CPI beat expectations on both measures. Headline rose 0.4% month over month against 0.3% expected, and core rose 0.3% against 0.2% expected.

Fed Funds futures, per Bloomberg calculations cited in the report, price a 100% chance of a 25 basis point hike in December. They price about an 80% chance of another 25 basis point hike in January. The report links this to the CPI data and hawkish FOMC rhetoric.
The 10-year and 30-year Treasury auctions both tailed, meaning they cleared at a higher yield than the market yield at the time of the auction. This added to the rise in yields.
Investment-grade corporate yields rose with benchmark yields. Spreads tightened by 1 to 3 basis points, so corporate yields rose slightly less than Treasury yields.
Municipal AAA yields rose 13 to 21 basis points, less than taxable yields. The largest moves were at the short end of the curve.

Brokered CD rates rose about 5 basis points across the curve. The average rate for 3-month to 1-year maturities rose to 4.43% from 4.37%, and for 2-year to 5-year maturities to 4.91% from 4.83%. Available issuers rose to 95 and total offerings rose from 143 to 165, concentrated at the front end.

Events this week: retail sales and industrial production on Tuesday, housing starts and FOMC minutes on Wednesday, jobless claims on Thursday, and University of Michigan survey data on Friday. FOMC Chair Warsh and other Fed members are scheduled to speak.

The report lists the Anthropic IPO, scheduled for this week, and the ongoing Nvidia story as technology headline risks. It also lists President Trump's Asia trip, including meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
